mission.title: litellm: [Bug]: /ui/chat returns 404 — Next.js static export missing index.html in chat/ directory
mission.description: [Bug]: /ui/chat returns 404 — Next.js static export missing index.html in chat/ directory. This issue affects 26+ users.

steps.title: Identify litellm troubleshoot symptoms
steps.description:
Check for the issue in your litellm deployment:
```bash
kubectl get pods -n litellm -l app.kubernetes.io/name=litellm
kubectl logs -l app.kubernetes.io/name=litellm -n litellm --tail=100 | grep -i error
```
Look for errors or warnings in the logs that may indicate the issue.

steps.title: Review litellm configuration
steps.description:
Inspect the relevant litellm configuration:
```bash
kubectl get all -n litellm -l app.kubernetes.io/name=litellm
kubectl get configmap -n litellm -l app.kubernetes.io/part-of=litellm
```
### Check for existing issues

### What happened?

Direct navigation to `/ui/chat` (or any UI sub-route like `/ui/logs`, `/ui/models-and-endpoints`) returns `{"detail":"Not Found"}` (HTTP 404).

steps.title: Generate index.html for each exported UI page directory
steps.description:
The Next.js static export emits `chat.html` instead of `chat/index.html`, so the proxy's static file handler finds nothing at `/ui/chat`. Fix it with a post-build step that creates a directory index for every exported page, then rebuild or patch the running image:
```bash
# Post-build step (run inside the UI build output directory, e.g. litellm/proxy/_experimental/out)
for f in *.html; do
  page="${f%.html}"
  [ "$page" = "index" ] && continue
  mkdir -p "$page"
  cp "$f" "$page/index.html"
done
```
Alternatively, add a catch-all route in the proxy that serves `{page}.html` when `{page}/index.html` is not found. Restart the litellm pods afterwards:
```bash
kubectl rollout restart statefulset/litellm -n litellm
```

steps.title: Confirm [Bug]: /ui/chat returns 404 — Next.js static… is resolved
steps.description:
Verify the fix by checking that the original error no longer occurs:
```bash
kubectl logs -l app.kubernetes.io/name=litellm -n litellm --tail=50 --since=5m
kubectl get events -n litellm --sort-by='.lastTimestamp' | tail -10
```
Confirm that the issue symptoms are gone.

resolution.summary: Direct navigation to /ui/chat returned 404 because the Next.js static export produces flat files (chat.html) rather than per-directory index files (chat/index.html), and the LiteLLM proxy's static handler only resolves directory index files. Copying each exported page to <page>/index.html (or adding a catch-all route that falls back to <page>.html) makes every UI sub-route resolvable on direct load, so bookmarks and refreshes on /ui/chat, /ui/logs and /ui/models-and-endpoints work again.

done

# Verify the fix
kubectl port-forward litellm-0 14000:4000
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://localhost:14000/ui/       # 200
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://localhost:14000/ui/chat   # 200 after fix
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://localhost:14000/ui/chat/  # 200 after fix
